newsitem.title: NORWAY: Kvaerner expects word on Woodside deal.
newsitem.headline: Kvaerner expects word on Woodside deal.

text.p: Norway's Kvaerner ASA group says it hopes to find out on Monday if it has won a 2.7 billion crown contract to build a floating production ship for Woodside Petroleum's Laminaria Field off Australia.

"I will get a visit from Woodside on Monday and I hope to receive word then that we are being awarded the contract, or get a timetable for when the matter has been clarified," project leader Tor Arne Aamodt of Kvaerner Oil & Gas told Reuters on Friday.
"We will have to wait until later in the week for the formalities that will clear the way for a press release," he said. "I am very optimistic."
A Norwegian newspaper, Dagens Naeringsliv, said last Saturday that Kvaerner's Oil & Gas division had landed the contract in competition with Brown & Root of the United States.
The newspaper said Woodside would announce the contract in mid-December.
London-based Kvaerner is among the bidders to supply Woodside with a floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) oil facility for the Laminaria oil field.
